segments.en:
The mock battle
will now begin.

Send the drill program to every
unit scheduled to sortie!
Sending the program now.
Oh, here it comes.

So far, so good!
You're doing great,
Lun!

Oh, Kanji...
Did it get to you all right?

Yeah!
It came through perfectly!
Um... Kanji?
What?

I went to the trouble of sending it,
so read it properly, okay?

Hahaha... (sweat)
I know, I know.

Okay then...
Guess I'll start up the program
Lun sent me.

So it starts with the basic controls?
What a pain~

But it's Lun asking me,
not just anyone.
Guess I'll just have to grin and bear it...

Heh...
I'll take a good long look at
how much those kids have grown.

We'll be entering attack range shortly.
All units, prepare to sortie!

All right, let's go,
my GT-K.

Nelfea! You probably know already,
but the enemy leader
is Kanji Akatsuki.

His machine is an FT,
the Cloud Saber.

If he flies at high altitude,
shooting him down with a ground-combat GT
is next to impossible.

I'll try provoking him, at least.
If he's the cocky type,
he might come down.

I wish I could've gotten you
an FT too, instead of a GT...

I don't mind.
I'm used to this machine.

Against Kanji, it's just
the right handicap.

Honestly...
what a girl you are...
Auntie Tail!

Don't treat me like a child
while I'm carrying out a mission...!

Ahaha...
I'm sorry.

But don't get the wrong idea.
I just thought you seemed
reliable, that's all.
Heh... Thanks.
It's almost time...
I'm launching!

Don't get cocky just because
you've got air superiority.

I'll show you what this
machine can really do!

We'll buy time with the GT-O
against attacks from the air!

Meanwhile, Nelfea,
charge in from the ground.
Roger!

Listen,
Big Bro.

In battle, whoever sinks the other
side's mothership first wins.

No matter how many units you have left,
if your mothership goes down, you lose.

Roger. So I just have to hit
the enemy mothership fast.

Also, the enemy mothership
has no units that are good
at aerial combat.

So you should take your
Cloud Saber and attack
from the air, Big Bro.

I know basic stuff like that
without you spelling it out
every single time.

Well, of course you do.
You ARE the "combat leader."
Okay, I'm counting on you!

All right!
Here I go!!
How's that!

You've gotten better,
Kanji!

But now
it's our turn.

Nelfea's unit has broken
through the defense line!

That leaves our
mothership wide open!

We have to launch
interceptors right away!

rows.notes: Battle tutorial; same scene as dlg_0672_07375_00 (other version) -- kept its terms: mock battle, drill program, mothership (UI), "combat leader" ([jp]), Auntie Tail. Seg 1 (no header): an order on Kanji's side, speaker unclear (likely Rie as captain). Seg 4 and 13 (no header) read as Kanji continuing. Seg 17 [jp] 'the enemy leader' (Kanji leads the opposing team). Seg 20 source has [jp] (requisition), clearly a typo for [jp] (provoke). Seg 23/26/28/33/35 (no header) read as the previous speaker continuing. Seg 47-49: 'How's that!' is Kanji; 'You've gotten better, Kanji!' has Nelfea's header (kept speaker-neutral). Seg 49 [jp] 'our turn' (Nelfea speaks for Tail's side). Seg 52 (no header): continues Rie's alarm. | [accuracy 6] subject restored: 'it' = the program Lun sent | [accuracy 13] [jp] = 'none other than Lun' (why he can't refuse); 'of all people' read as surprise/disparagement | [accuracy 24] [jp] is exasperated admiration (Tail says next she meant Nelfea seemed reliable); 'you're such a kid' made it an insult and contradicted k28. 'girl' still lets Nelfea take it as being treated like a child | [accuracy 30] [jp] = 'almost time'; 'It's about time' reads as impatient 'finally' | [accuracy 31] subject restored (Nelfea launching herself) | [editorial 4] 'Going smoothly, smoothly!' was a literal doubling | [editorial 12] Kanji is alone: 'We're' had no referent; the program is the subject (accuracy flag k12) | [editorial 21] word order: 'too' attached to the FT, as accuracy flag k21 suggested | [editorial 45] 'Well' repeated from k44 'Well, of course you do.'
